title: Machine Learning and AI Engineer
summary: ML and AI engineers build, deploy and maintain models and AI features, from classic ML to apps built on large language models. It suits students who like both programming and maths and want to ship working software.

nodes.title: Python programming
nodes.summary: Get comfortable with Python: functions, classes, modules, files and errors, plus NumPy and pandas. ML engineers write real software, so clean code matters as much as models.
nodes.proof: A small Python package with functions, tests and a README that cleans and summarises a dataset, on GitHub.

sources.title: Machine Learning Crash Course: Prerequisites and prework – Google

nodes.title: Maths for ML: linear algebra and statistics
nodes.summary: Learn vectors, matrices, derivatives, probability and basic statistics with a focus on intuition. These explain how training, loss and gradients work.
nodes.proof: Implement gradient descent for linear regression with NumPy and plot the loss going down over iterations.

sources.title: Machine Learning Crash Course: Prerequisites and prework – Google

nodes.title: Machine learning fundamentals
nodes.summary: Learn regression, classification, trees and clustering, how to split data, avoid overfitting and choose metrics. Use scikit-learn to practise on real datasets.

resources.title: Machine Learning Crash Course – Google for Developers
Introduction to Machine Learning – NPTEL (IIT Madras)

nodes.proof: A scikit-learn pipeline with preprocessing, cross-validation and hyperparameter search, with a short note on the chosen metric.

sources.title: Machine Learning Crash Course – Google for Developers
Datasets, generalization, and overfitting – Google MLCC

nodes.title: Deep learning with PyTorch
nodes.summary: Learn tensors, autograd, building and training neural networks, and saving models in PyTorch. Then try a computer vision or NLP task with a pretrained model.

resources.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders – fast.ai
Intro to Deep Learning – Kaggle Learn

nodes.proof: Fine-tune a pretrained image or text model on your own small dataset and report accuracy on a held-out test set.

nodes.title: LLMs and generative AI apps
nodes.summary: Learn how transformers and LLMs work, how to use them through libraries and APIs, and how to build retrieval-augmented (RAG) apps and simple agents. Many AI engineer roles focus on this.

resources.title: Introduction to Large Language Models – Google MLCC

nodes.proof: A small RAG app that answers questions over a set of documents and shows which passages it used.

nodes.title: Serving models: APIs and Docker
nodes.summary: Wrap a trained model in a small web API, package it with Docker and run it anywhere. Use Git for all your code. Employers want models that run outside a notebook.
nodes.proof: A Docker image that serves predictions from your model over HTTP, with run instructions in the README.

nodes.title: Production ML and MLOps basics
nodes.summary: Learn what happens after deployment: data validation, tracking experiments, monitoring for drift and retraining. This is the gap between a demo and a product.
nodes.proof: Add logging of inputs and predictions to your served model and a simple script that flags when input data shifts.

nodes.title: End-to-end ML or AI project
nodes.summary: Build one project from data to deployed app: train or adapt a model, serve it, add a simple front end and monitoring. One finished, deployed project beats many half-done notebooks.

resources.title: AI and Data Scientist Projects – roadmap.sh

nodes.proof: A public GitHub repo plus a live demo or video, with a README covering the problem, data, model, metrics and limits.

nodes.title: Interview preparation and applying
nodes.summary: Revise ML concepts and metrics, practise Python coding questions and data structures problems, and prepare an ML system design answer (such as a recommender). Rehearse explaining your project.

resources.title: Top 60+ Data Science Interview Questions – roadmap.sh
Top 30 System Design Interview Questions – roadmap.sh

nodes.proof: Do two mock interviews: one on ML concepts and coding, one where you design an ML system on a whiteboard.

sources.title: Top 60+ Data Science Interview Questions – roadmap.sh
